key_insight: Global optimal control can strongly suppress decoherence in globally driven superconducting quantum architectures by reshaping the drive in time, enabling high-fidelity operations even when all qubits are exposed to noise.
engineering_relevance: For scalable quantum processors using global drives, pulse shaping can cut gate times by about an order of magnitude while preserving gate fidelity, improving practicality under realistic decoherence.
method: Model a quasi-2D ladder architecture as a prototype globally driven superconducting platform.
Use tensor-network simulations to track quantum-information flow under amplitude damping and dephasing.
Apply global optimal control to reshape the drive and compress one- and two-qubit gate sequences.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evaluation of decoherence effects on information flow and gate fidelity, and shows that optimized global drive shaping restores high fidelities while reducing gate duration by roughly 10×.
watch_item: Because dissipation acts on the entire globally driven device, the mitigation depends on precise pulse optimization and may be challenging to generalize without platform-specific control calibration.
paper_title: Mitigating quantum decoherence via global optimal control
